assertions.name: volume_factor_more_than_halves_scatter
assertions.source: The defensible claim the data supports: introducing the template's Vol^(-1/3) factor (either proxy) more than halves the scatter in the implied per-pair crossing number versus no volume factor at all.

assertions.name: pair_locality_no_significant_correlation
assertions.source: Pair-locality requires C to be uncorrelated with the proton-pair count; |r| stays below the n=4 significance threshold.

description: EXPLORATORY test of the Freedman-He asymptotic-crossing-number template for the open two-like-charge EM-linking invariant (bean qou-0hdx). The topological routes are closed (O1 antisymmetry, Flux^3 scaling, Brunnian vanishing); the crossing number is unsigned, symmetric, Flux^2, and carries Khesin Thm 3.6's Vol^(-1/3) template. Under that reading the implied per-pair crossing number C = kappa*A^(1/3) must be CONSTANT (pair topology is local) and UNCORRELATED with the proton-pair count. Both are tested; the 1/3 exponent is fixed by the template, not tuned. Nothing wired.

pair_locality_check.significance_note: With n = 4, |r| must exceed ~0.95 to be significant at the 5% level; neither correlation reaches that, so the data are CONSISTENT with pair-locality but cannot establish it.

data.verdict: The Freedman-He proxy is NOT the most constant reading (best: alt: Vol ~ Z (proton content)). That counts against the Vol^(-1/3) template as stated.
data.what_would_close_it: Compute the asymptotic crossing number of the proton pair in the corpus's own Borromean braid geometry and check it against the implied constant. That is a topological computation on a known configuration -- no new physics input -- and it is the step that would turn this consistency into a derivation. Independently, extending the kappa(A) table to A ~ 27-57 (bean qou-i6rg) separates this Vol^(-1/3) reading from the coth-saturation alternative, which predicts the opposite large-A limit.
data.failed_prediction_recorded: The first version of this probe asserted that the Freedman-He proxy (Vol ~ A) would be the MOST constant reading. It is NOT: Vol ~ Z scores 5.1702178% against A's 6.1004926%. That assertion failed and is recorded here rather than quietly dropped. The honest reading is that a volume factor of SOME kind is doing real work (both proxies ~5-6% vs 17% with none), but four points cannot discriminate A from Z -- and Z is physically defensible, since the domain relevant to a proton-pair Coulomb energy is arguably the proton subsystem rather than the whole nucleus. Which volume enters the template is now an explicit open sub-question, not a settled input.
